html:
The Wappo, who call themselves Micewal, are a Native American people of the Napa Valley and nearby valleys north of San Francisco Bay, reaching to the south shore of Clear Lake and the Alexander and Russian River valleys. Their language is distantly related to that of the Yuki to the north, from whom they seem to have split at least 500 years ago. The name Wappo is usually said to come from Spanish guapo, "brave".

They lived in villages by streams and hot springs, gathering acorns, hunting and trading with their Pomo and Patwin neighbours. They resisted the Mexican settlers of Sonoma in the 1830s and fought several clashes with their troops. The mission at Sonoma, founded in 1823, drew some in, and smallpox in 1838 killed many. The Gold Rush years and the growth of Napa's farms took the rest of their land.
